title: Bounded complexes of flat sheaves have tor amplitude
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme, $\Lambda$ a commutative ring, $a,b\in\mathbf Z$ with $a\le b$, and let $\mathcal E^\bullet$ be a bounded
complex of flat $\Lambda_T$-module sheaves supported in degrees
$[a,b]$. Then $\mathcal E^\bullet$, regarded as an object of
$D(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$, has tor amplitude in $[a,b]$
([def-kun-tor-amplitude]).

proof.text:
A bounded-above complex of flat $\Lambda_T$-module sheaves is K-flat
by [lem-kun-kflat-criteria](1), so by
[def-kun-derived-tensor] the derived tensor product
$\mathcal E^\bullet\kunotimes{\Lambda}\mathcal M$ is computed by the
ordinary tensor product $\mathcal E^\bullet\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal M$, whose terms in degrees outside
$[a,b]$ vanish. Hence
$H^i\bigl(\mathcal E^\bullet\kunotimes{\Lambda}\mathcal M\bigr)=0$
for every $i\notin[a,b]$ and every $\Lambda_T$-module sheaf
$\mathcal M$ placed in degree zero, which is tor amplitude in
$[a,b]$ by [def-kun-tor-amplitude].

lean.statement:
lemma torAmplitudeIn_Q_obj_of_flat (P : CochainComplex C ℤ) (a b : ℤ)
    [P.IsStrictlyGE a] [P.IsStrictlyLE b] (hP : ∀ n, ObjectProperty.flat (P.X n)) :
    torAmplitudeIn C a b (Q.obj P)
lean.note: Specialize C to Sheaf T.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ), for T : Scheme.{u} and Λ : Type (u + 1), [CommRing Λ]. CochainComplex.isStrictlyGE_iff and isStrictlyLE_iff identify the support hypotheses with zero terms outside [a,b]; hP is exactness of sheaf tensor with every term. No extra geometric or coefficient hypotheses are required: the etale module-sheaf category has the structural instances of the generic theorem. The node assumes a ≤ b; the existing theorem also covers a > b, when the support conditions force the zero complex, so its specialization at ordered endpoints is exactly the requested assertion. AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.DerivedCategory.hasTorAmplitudeIn_iff_torAmplitudeIn in WeilConjectures.SixFunctors.Etale.Derived.Finiteness.FlatModel identifies the conclusion with the bounded-interval predicate recorded by def-kun-tor-amplitude. The latter etale torAmplitudeIn is an abbreviation for this generic predicate. Both declarations and their surrounding hypotheses were independently read; no duplicate theorem is needed.
